pr_title: Handle default body text when creating issues and pull requests
pr_body:
This comment refers to the original description: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/3658#pullrequestreview-663009869

This fixes #674.

After a second look at the code, `surveyext.GhEditor` explicitly returns an empty string when pressing `Enter`.  It doesn't look like it had anything to do with unwritten temporary files. I added an extra if clause to see if the editor prompt was instructed to add the default value to the editor.

Unfortunately, adding tests for this isn't straightforward and, so far, no tests exist for `survey.GhEditor`.  If you still want me to try to add tests, let me know.

The `GhEditor` is used in these cases:

- `gh issue create`
- `gh issue edit`
- `gh pr create`
- `gh pr edit`
- `gh pr review`

`gh issue create` and `gh pr create` are the only places where the new condition will trigger.  The original behavior (returning an empty string when skipping) seem to be preserved everywhere else.
pr_comments: I think this fix is done.  The one additional thing I did was convert the list of if statements for detecting keyboard presses to a switch statement (commit 6db87ff56f199fd8022d80154d9ed38687a099ff).
Hi @mislav!  I'm just checking to see if there is something else I need to fix in this pull request.  It looks like `pr-auto` is failing because of how I edited my pull request description, I think?

Understood.  Thanks for adding the tests and for merging!

Do those renamings or refactorings manifest as separate issues that I can contribute to or do those kinds of issues get taken care of periodically by the core team?

@chemotaxis We periodically address technical debt by refactoring and shuffling code around, of course! We are open to receiving those kinds of contributions as well, but keep in mind that we expect that a refactoring yields some tangible improvement (e.g. that the new code is slimmer, or easier to test, or more portable, or more resilient against edge cases) and that the author is mindful of potential regressions (e.g. avoids changes to code that has little test coverage). Otherwise, if a change is purely cosmetic, such as renaming a struct field (even if the new name is slightly more descriptive), we are less keen on accepting those since the risk-to-benefit ratio isn't in our favor.

issue_context.title: gh pr create doesn't autofill commit body when skipping body
issue_context.body: I was doing some QAing of the latest release and noticed that when I followed these steps the body didn't autofill as I expected: 1. Made a single commit with a title and body: `git commit -m "Title" -m "Body" --allow-empty` 1. `gh pr create` 1. accepted auto filled title 1. `Enter` to skip 1. Submit The resulting PR was missing the body: When I did the same process, and used `e` to view it in the editor first, it worked. I would expect to be able to use enter to skip and it would still autofill Let me know if I can provide any more context!
comments:
Good catch! I wonder if @vilmibm might have chosen this by design? 

In my head, I could make a case that either behavior is correct. The behavior that you're seeing, for example, makes sense to me if I think of it in the way that while git commit information is used to _pre-populate_ the editor, it won't be submitted as-is if I have neither edited it nor had a chance to preview what would be submitted.

Yeah I could see both cases! But I actually feel pretty strongly on this one that it should still populate when you skip, since I think the use case is that people _know_ they inputted title and body already and just want to submit as quickly as possible, using `enter` `enter` `submit`.
@ampinsk Do you still feel the same way about the behavior of this interaction? If so, I am happy to pick up and implement this.
Yes that would be great, thank you @wilso199!

@wilso199 
I was facing a similar situation when I was trying to fix #1294 and #1219 
I was thinking of having our editor prompt give 2 options, instead of just our current `<enter> to skip`  
It would be something like `<enter> to keep empty and <d> to select default`

This is because 'skip' essentially is a bit ambiguous, and different users expect it to behave differently(empty/default).
empty and default would be a bit more precise, and both are actually relevant options according to me

If you are going to do this change, let me know, so that I will wait for you to do it, and then merge it in my upcoming PR to solve #1294  
Otherwise, I am as it is going to do this change in my PR

Thanks

cc @ampinsk @mislav
@AliabbasMerchant I see you have already started working on this. I will let you add the change to your PR. Thank you for letting me know!
Cool, thanks @wilso199 (so now my PR will attempt to solve 3 issues at the same time :laughing: :sweat_smile: ) [Lets hope I do not make any mistakes :sweat_smile: ]

We have since discovered that this bug affects the `--recover` flow as well, so I'm bumping up the severity.

Also, forwarding @waldyrious' suggestion from #3282:

> Maybe showing an excerpt of the previously written body as a greyed out default for the body text (the same way it is done for the title) could help make this flow predictable.
Is anyone already working on this? If not, I would take a look at fixing this 😃.

review_comments: Let me know if you'd like a nested if statement or just keep the flat if statement.
You are welcome to restructure the conditional logic to something that would be more cleaner in your view.
It also might make sense to rename `BlankAllowed` to something like `SkipEditorAllowed`, since skipping no longer just returns an empty string.
Makes sense to me too! Thanks for looking into this
Sure!  This is taken care of in commit 6497114a864da1ddb9a52031d67d7bbba523bf10.
